messages:
Samir: Quick question — Acme hybrid setup: they bought Dedicated reserved capacity in us-west1 from us *and* have on-prem nodes in their NYC colo. How do we show pass-through on their monthly invoice for: GPU licensing (vendor license fees), cloud egress, and KMS? Do we pro-rate committed discounts, or is Dedicated treated as a fixed line?
Maria: Short answer: Dedicated reserved capacity = fixed committed fee we bill (monthly/annual commit). Pass-through applies to third-party bills we pay on behalf of the customer (e.g., if we run the customer's cloud account or if contract says pass-through). For on-prem vendor license invoices (eg NVidia/ISV) we usually pass-through if the SOW/PO calls it out. Otherwise we absorb/allocate under support. Need the SOW id to be sure. :clipboard:
Anjali: From ops side — we can produce the usage export for both clouds + onprem agent. Example command for last month:
```
/opt/redwood/bin/usage-export --scope acme-corp --start 2026-02-01 --end 2026-02-28 --format csv > acme-202602-usage.csv
```
That CSV has GPU_hours, egress_gb, kms_calls per node/region.
Ken: We recommend invoicing pass-through as explicit line items. Formula we use: 
```
GPU_license_pass = SUM(gpu_hours_customer) * LICENSE_RATE_PER_GPU_HOUR
Egress_pass = SUM(egress_gb_customer) * EGRESS_RATE_PER_GB
KMS_pass = (kms_api_calls / 1e6) * KMS_RATE_PER_1M
```
Example numbers (illustrative): GPU hours=1,200 -> 1200 * $0.10 = $120. Egress=4,500 GB -> 4500 * $0.085 = $382.50.
NYC-Ops: A nuance on committed discounts — if the Dedicated commit is sold to the customer (they reserved capacity from us), we list it as a fixed committed capacity fee (no pro-rating of cloud provider discounts). Pro-rating only matters when we buy committed-use discounts from cloud provider and *we* are charging multiple customers from a pooled commitment — that model is rare and needs explicit contract terms.
Maria: Policy recap: 
- If customer runs in their cloud account (we didn't pay provider) -> we don't pass through provider egress/KMS; they see their own bill.
- If Redwood provisions cloud resources under our account for a Private deployment and we pay the provider -> we pass-through cloud line-items (egress, network nat, KMS) if included in SOW/contract.
- Vendor license invoices (NVIDIA, ISV drivers) -> pass-through only if the contract states so; otherwise amortize into support/managed services.
Please add SOW/PO id in the ticket and we can generate the draft invoice template.
billing-bot: Draft invoice (preview) for acme-corp created: https://invoices.redwood.internal/drafts/ACME-202602 (contains platform fee, dedicated commit line, and provisional pass-through lines — pending attach of vendor invoice).
Samir: Great — next steps for me: 1) grab last month CSV, 2) confirm SOW clause for license pass-through, 3) attach vendor invoice if available. @Anjali can you upload the CSV + a quick summary to the secure bucket?
Anjali: On it. Uploaded to gs://redwood-secure/acme-corp/billing/2026-02/acme-202602-usage.csv and set ACL to finance-read. Also dropped a short summary in the bucket at acme-202602-summary.txt. Pinged with link in #secure-files.
Samir: Perfect, I'll open a billing PR and reference the SOW. Maria/Ken — any preferences for how we label license pass-through on the invoice ("GPU license (vendor pass-through)" vs "Third-party GPU license")?
Maria: Use "Third-party GPU license (pass-through)" — clarity for audits. Also add original vendor invoice ref number in invoice notes.
Ken: Agreed. Also recommend adding a small footnote about committed capacity: "Dedicated reserved capacity is a Redwood commitment and billed as a fixed fee per SOW; cloud-provider discounts applied by Redwood are internal and not itemized unless specified."
Samir: Thanks all — I'll proceed and tag you on the PR. :thumbsup:
